title: Add adaptive SLA-aware traffic corking guard for performance canaries
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: During gradual rollout canaries we sometimes see transient tail-latency spikes caused by bursty background traffic or long-tailed user flows. These spikes increase noise for detectors and can cause unnecessary rollbacks or user-visible SLA violations. This PR adds an adaptive, SLA-aware traffic corking guard that temporarily reduces (corks) low-priority traffic fraction when the canary signals tail-latency pressure, preserving capacity for high-priority requests and stabilizing canary signals.

Design summary: corking is an automated, short-lived traffic shaping action performed by the perf-canary controller. The guard monitors per-route 95/99/99.9 latency, in-flight concurrency, and SLA budget (error budget / latency SLO burn rate). When the guard detects sustained tail-latency elevation above configured thresholds AND the estimated SLA burn suggests user-facing impact, it computes a cork fraction in [0.0, 0.9] to reduce non-critical traffic classes. Corking is adaptive: fraction depends on severity and remaining SLA budget; duration is bounded and decays automatically. The controller uses exponential backoff for repeated corks to avoid oscillation.

Key configuration knobs (defaults included): policy.sla_window_seconds=60, policy.tail_latency_ms_thresholds={p95:150,p99:400,p999:1200}, policy.min_cork_fraction=0.1, policy.max_cork_fraction=0.6, policy.cooldown_seconds=120, policy.priority_classes=["user","interactive","batch","background"], policy.cork_targets=["background","batch"]. These are mounted as CRD fields for Redwood Private and as remote flags in hosted.

Implementation notes: - New controller: perf-canary/controllers/traffic_corker.py implements the temporal decision logic and exposes a TrialCork CRD used internally by the controller manager. The cork action translates to a traffic-shaping directive in the router (via existing traffic-mutation API) that temporarily drops or deprioritizes a percentage of requests in the targeted priority classes. - Integration with canary pipeline: the corker subscribes to canary health streams (latency histograms and throughput) and emits events consumed by the rollout manager so the rollout can pause or continue based on combined signal. - Observability: added metrics corker.actions_total, corker.current_fraction, corker.cooldowns, and a dedicated dashboard and alert rule to detect repeated cork storms. - Safety: default policy only corks non-user-facing classes and requires a linear ticket (ENG-) opt-in to extend to higher priority classes.

Testing and benchmarks: added unit tests for decision heuristics and a small integration harness that simulates mixed traffic (80% background/batch, 20% user) with injected tail events. Benchmarks against a baseline canary run show a 5-9% reduction in p99-p999 tail spikes under identical synthetic bursts and reduced false-positive rate for the canary detector in our replay tests.

Rollout plan: gated by feature flag perf.corker.enabled. Start with internal SRE on dedicated clusters: 0% -> 10% of routes (1 week) -> 50% (observability window) -> 100%. We also added a kill-switch in the control plane to immediately disable corking globally.

Security & compliance: corker does not touch request payloads or logs, only traffic metadata and routing weights. All actions are audited and appear in existing audit logs.

What this PR contains: - controller, tests, CRD stubs, router adapter, docs, dashboard changes, quickstart policy example.

Checklist: [x] unit tests, [x] integration replay, [x] dashboard + alerts, [x] docs, [x] release notes, [x] feature-flag gating.

review_comments: Diego Ramos (reviewer): Can the corker accidentally mask a real regression in the canary by hiding bad behavior? Please add rationale and a telemetry signal to detect masking.
Maya Patel (author): Added a masking-detection metric (corker.masking_risk) and a conservative rule that increases cork only if masking_risk is below 0.2. Documented in docs/operator/corker.md.
Leah Kim (reviewer): The cooldown/backoff logic looks reasonable but needs an explicit unit test for repeated corks across windows.
Maya Patel (author): Added test 'test_corker_repeated_cork_backoff' in perf-canary/tests/test_corker.py and extended integration replay.

release_notes: New feature: adaptive SLA-aware traffic corking guard. Helps stabilize canary signals by temporarily reducing non-critical traffic when tail-latency threatens SLAs. Gated by feature flag perf.corker.enabled; operator opt-in required for private clusters.
risk_profile: Medium: impacts routing decisions for low-priority traffic. Defaults are conservative and feature-flag gated. Auditing and kill-switch added.
notes_for_ops: Operators should watch corker.actions_total and corker.masking_risk during rollout. Use control-plane kill-switch if unexpected user impact observed. Default policy only targets background/batch classes.
follow_up: ENG-4921 follow-up: add multi-route correlation to avoid simultaneous corks across dependent routes; SRE-230: tune thresholds based on customer traffic shapes.
